questions.q: A driver stopped his vehicle in a permitted place, opened the rear door, unloaded a crate and closed the door immediately, without turning off the engine and without a break. What is this action?
questions.explain: Immediate, continuous unloading of goods, without a break, is standing — not parking (reg. 1).

questions.q: What is the difference between standing and parking under the law?
options: Standing is allowed only by day, parking only at night
Standing is allowed only for a private car
Standing is a continuous, immediate stop to pick up or set down passengers, or to load or unload goods; parking is any other way of leaving the vehicle standing
There is no legal difference between the two
questions.explain: Parking is defined as leaving the vehicle standing for any length of time, other than for the immediate, continuous pick-up/set-down of passengers or loading/unloading of goods — which is exactly standing (reg. 1).

questions.q: What distinguishes stopping from standing and from parking?
options: Stopping is a temporary break in the journey where the driver waits to move on immediately, and does not really leave the vehicle
Stopping exists only at a traffic light
Stopping is forbidden in every case and every place
There is no difference between stopping and parking
questions.explain: A short stop — such as at a red light, at a Stop sign, or to give way — is not parking, because the driver remains ready to move on immediately.

questions.q: What is the difference between sign 432 and sign 433?
options: There is no difference, the two signs are identical
Sign 432 also forbids a short stop to set down passengers; sign 433 allows it
Sign 432 prohibits parking only and permits a short stop, loading/unloading and picking up/setting down passengers; sign 433 prohibits all three actions
questions.explain: Sign 432 prohibits parking only. Sign 433 is stricter — it prohibits stopping and standing as well.

questions.q: On a stretch of road that looks forbidden under the general rules, a sign is placed that permits parking. What decides?
options: The general rules apply only at night
This is a mistake — a sign can never permit something in a forbidden place
A sign that permits stopping, standing or parking overrides the general prohibition in the regulations
questions.explain: Regulation 76(a): you may stop, stand or park anywhere a sign permits it, even if the general rule forbids it.

questions.q: At what distance before a pedestrian crossing is it forbidden to stop, stand or park a vehicle?
questions.explain: You may not stop, stand or park a vehicle within {{fact:park.no_stop.pedestrian_crossing_m}} before a pedestrian crossing (regulation 72(a)(6)).

questions.q: What is the forbidden distance for stopping, standing and parking before and after a railway level crossing?
questions.explain: The prohibition applies within {{fact:park.no_stop.railway_crossing_m}} before the nearest rail and after it (regulation 72(a)(8)).

questions.q: Up to how many metres before a bridge or a tunnel, and within them, is stopping, standing and parking forbidden?
questions.explain: The prohibition applies on the bridge or in the tunnel itself, and also {{fact:park.no_stop.bridge_tunnel_m}} before and after them (regulation 72(a)(11)).

questions.q: What does a kerb painted black-and-white mean?
options: Just a highly visible marking for kerbs and traffic islands — it is not a parking ban
questions.explain: Black-and-white is purely a visual marking. Thinking it is a parking ban is a common misconception.

questions.q: In which of the following cases is parking forbidden, regardless of any specific numeric distance?
options: Right next to another vehicle that is already standing or parked at the side of the road
questions.explain: You may not stop, stand or park a vehicle beside another vehicle that is already standing or parked at the side of the road (regulation 72(a)(10)).

questions.q: When may you stop or park on the side of the road opposite a bus stop?
options: If the road there is at least {{fact:park.bus_stop.opposite_min_width}} wide
questions.explain: When the road is {{fact:park.bus_stop.opposite_min_width}} wide or more, you may stop or park on the side opposite the bus stop (regulation 72(a)(12)).

questions.q: In parallel parking, what is the maximum permitted distance between the wheels nearest the kerb and the kerb itself?
questions.explain: Regulation 75 sets a maximum distance of {{fact:park.curb_distance_max}} between the wheels nearest the kerb and the kerb.

questions.q: A vehicle is parked on a steep downhill slope. How should the front wheels be turned, and what gear should be engaged?
options: There is no difference between uphill and downhill
Wheels toward the kerb, reverse gear
Wheels toward the road, forward gear
questions.explain: Going downhill, turn the front wheels toward the kerb or the edge of the road, and engage reverse gear — so that if the vehicle moves, it will be stopped by the kerb (regulation 74(c)).

questions.q: Before opening the door of a parked vehicle, what must you do?
options: Look back and take every precaution needed to keep road users safe
questions.explain: Regulation 80: you must not open a vehicle door without first taking every precaution needed — especially because of cyclists and motorcyclists passing the vehicle.

questions.q: Before leaving a vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: Leave the engine running to keep it cool
Turn off the engine, remove the ignition key, and apply the parking brake
questions.explain: Regulation 74: an unattended vehicle must have the engine off, the ignition key removed, and the standing brakes (parking brake) applied.

questions.q: When is angled or perpendicular parking allowed, instead of parallel to the road?
options: Only where the local signage authority has permitted it and marked it for angled parking
questions.explain: The default is parallel parking along the edge of the road (regulation 75). Angled parking is allowed only where it has been permitted and marked.

questions.q: What is special about sign 437?
options: It forbids parking for all vehicles
It reserves a parking spot for a vehicle carrying a valid disabled badge, while it is serving the badge holder
questions.explain: Sign 437 reserves the parking spot for a vehicle with a valid disabled badge, while the vehicle is actually serving the person the badge was issued to.

questions.q: What is the fine for blocking a vehicle carrying a disabled badge that is lawfully parked in a disabled parking spot?
questions.explain: Blocking a vehicle with a disabled badge in its reserved spot brings a fine of {{fine:parking-disabled-blocking}}.

questions.q: What does a kerb painted with alternating blue mean?
options: Paid parking is allowed, under sign 439 alongside sign 626 or 627
Parking reserved for disabled drivers only
questions.explain: An alternating blue kerb marks paid parking, at the tariff and hours given on the nearby signs.

questions.q: What does a kerb painted red-and-yellow permit?
options: Parking for any vehicle for an unlimited time
An absolute stopping ban for all vehicles
Stopping only, for the type of vehicle stated on the sign above it, to pick up/set down passengers or to load/unload
questions.explain: Red-and-yellow permits stopping only for the type of vehicle allowed by the sign, and only to pick up and set down passengers — not for parking.

questions.q: When may a vehicle stand or park on the carriageway or the shoulder of a non-urban road marked as a main or regional road?
options: Only in cases defined by law — such as picking up passengers on the shoulder, rescue, public works, or an unavoidable breakdown
questions.explain: Regulation 69(a)-(e) forbids this almost entirely on such roads, apart from the specific cases the law lists.

questions.q: From what minimum distance must the warning triangle be visible to a vehicle approaching from behind?
questions.explain: Regulation 70(a): the warning triangle must be placed so it can be seen by a vehicle approaching from behind from at least {{fact:equip.triangle.visibility}} away.

questions.q: A works vehicle, bus or goods vehicle whose permitted gross weight exceeds what figure must show a flashing amber lamp or hazard lights when standing outside town during lighting-up time?
questions.explain: Regulation 70(b): above {{fact:equip.hazard_lights_heavy}}, a flashing amber lamp or all the direction indicators together are required.

questions.q: When must you wear a high-visibility vest when getting out of the vehicle because of a breakdown?
options: When getting out of the vehicle on a non-urban road — by day and by night alike
Only if the police asked for it
questions.explain: Traffic Ordinance, section 65B(c): the duty to wear a vest when getting out of the vehicle on a non-urban road applies always, not only in darkness.

questions.q: Your vehicle has broken down outside town. What is the safest practice while waiting for help?
options: Stand well away from the road and the flow of traffic, beyond the safety barrier if there is one
Stand beside the vehicle on the traffic side to be seen clearly
Stay seated in the vehicle with the seatbelt on, without getting out at all
Stand behind the vehicle on the carriageway to stop approaching vehicles
questions.explain: Vehicles that hit the stranded vehicle could also hit anyone standing next to it. The safe place to wait is well away from the road and the traffic.
